extracted.title: Keys on Doormats: Exposed API Credentials on the Web
extracted.venue: arXiv 2603.12498, v3 of 14 September 2026; the v3 text states publication in the proceedings of ACM CCS '26 (15 to 19 November 2026). Screened as an arXiv preprint on search metadata
extracted.inclusion: included (Part A): removal and revocation of exposed API credentials, with and without notification by the authors; outcomes are exposure persistence and counts removed or revoked; method stated. The notification's outcome is credential removal or revocation, not patching, so the LH060 exclusion does not apply
extracted.population: 1,748 verified credentials for 14 providers found in HTTP Archive's September 2025 crawl of about 10 million websites; persistence from nine HTTP Archive snapshots; disclosure monitoring daily for 14 days and on day 172
extracted.data_public: input crawl public (HTTP Archive); credential data not public, as expected
outcome_facts: "exposed credentials remain publicly accessible for an average of 12 months (min: 1; SD: 14; max: 60)"; "In the first month after exposure, we observe a 10% reduction in the number of active credentials" (Section 5.6)
After disclosure: "exposures reducing 50% from 1,405 (Day 0) to 706 (Day 14)"; verified credential exposures "dropping from 1,175 to 865", "about 26% within 14 days" (Section 6.1)
"total non-removed exposures increase from 706 (Day 14) to 1,019 (Day 172) but non-revoked exposure counts show a further decrease from 865 (Day 14) to 660 (Day 172)" (Section 6.1)
"AWS credentials have the highest revocations (122 revocations or 55%) while Telegram and Bitly credentials are the two least revoked ones, with only 1 revocation each" (Section 6.1)
extracted.anonymisation_note: The paper describes affected organisations at a general level; Lighthouse records nothing that could identify them.
